findings.title: Data read + external network = exfiltration path
findings.description: Tools that can read internal data AND make external network requests create a direct exfiltration channel. A hijacked agent could read sensitive data then forward it to an attacker-controlled endpoint. Provided by: detect_workplace_programs (data_read) + detect_workplace_programs (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Credential access + external network = credential theft path
findings.description: Tools that access credentials AND make external requests can exfiltrate tokens, API keys, and secrets to remote servers. Provided by: detect_workplace_programs (credential_access) + detect_workplace_programs (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Broad data read + write = data manipulation risk
findings.description: Tools that can both read and write data could be manipulated to corrupt, overwrite, or delete information. Provided by: detect_workplace_programs (data_read) + detect_workplace_programs (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Filesystem access + external network = file exfiltration path
findings.description: Tools that access local files AND make network requests can exfiltrate source code, configs, keys, and documents. Provided by: detect_workplace_programs (filesystem) + detect_workplace_programs (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Credential access + data write = privilege persistence
findings.description: Tools that access credentials AND write data could persist stolen credentials or create backdoor accounts. Provided by: detect_workplace_programs (credential_access) + detect_workplace_programs (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Unpinned install source
findings.description: `npx @mambalabsdev/mcp-workplace-program-detector` without a pinned version in .mcp.json at line 4. Without an exact version the next install silently picks up whatever is published, including a compromised release.
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact version (pkg@1.2.3, pkg==1.2.3) and prefer a lockfile or hash-checked requirements.

findings.title: No logging found in files that define MCP tools (low confidence)
findings.description: None of the tool-defining files (src\index.ts) reference a logging library or logger call. Tool invocations may leave no audit trail. Confidence is low: logging could be configured elsewhere or by the host.
findings.recommendation: Log each tool invocation (tool name, caller/session, outcome, and redacted arguments) to a durable, tamper-evident sink.

findings.title: Blast radius: HIGH — compromise of this server has broad impact
findings.description: If this MCP server is compromised, the blast radius is HIGH due to: external network access, filesystem access, credential access. A single tool poisoning or supply chain attack could cascade across all connected systems.
findings.recommendation: Apply least-privilege to this server. Isolate it from other MCP servers. Implement kill switches and behavioral monitoring. Limit env vars to the minimum required.

tools.name: detect_workplace_programs
tools.description: Detect which people programs a company publishes on its own surfaces, and return one flat row per domain. It reads two independent paths and each catches what the other misses: the company's live job postings through its Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board, which is where benefits language that marketing pages omit shows up, and the careers, culture, benefits, DEI and ESG pages on the website, which is where employee resource group and volunteering language shows up. Either path can be turned off. If you already know the company's ATS board slug, pass ats_slug to skip discovery and read that board directly. Results are cached for 14 days and skipCache forces a fresh crawl. This reports what a company publishes, which is not the same as what it does: absence of a signal means the company does not say it publicly, not that the program does not exist. Requires an APIFY_TOKEN and consumes Apify credits. Read only: it reads public pages, it writes nothing.

domain.description: Bare domain, for example hubspot.com. Protocol and path are stripped.

ats_slug.description: Skip ATS discovery and read this Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board slug directly.

programs.description: Report only these program families. Omit for all six. A family you do not select reports null on its boolean, its evidence URL and its evidence phrase, never false, and is not counted in program_count. A selected family that is genuinely absent still reports false. Narrowing does not make a run cheaper: the corpus is the same either way, only the matching is narrowed.

scan_job_postings.description: Reads the company's live job bodies from its ATS. This path finds benefits language that marketing pages omit. Default: true.

scan_web_pages.description: Probes the careers, culture, benefits, DEI and ESG paths. This path finds ERG and volunteering language that job postings omit. Default: true.

max_pages.description: Sent as a string for Clay. Clamped to 1 to 25. Default: "14".

skipCache.description: false uses the 14 day cache, true forces a fresh crawl. Sent as a string for Clay, matching the fleet convention. Default: "false".

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
